steps.label: Step 0 - Analysis Depth
steps.description: Choose how deep the interview should go. Starter = tech only. Standard = + domain. Deep = + quality.

options.label: Standard
options.description: Starter + Domain Deep-Dive with entities, personas, stories. 90 minutes.

options.label: Deep
options.description: Standard + Quality, Security, Deploy, DevOps, Process. 3 hours.

steps.label: Step 1 - Domain Sketch
steps.description: Quick context to inform technology choices. 5 fields, 2 minutes. These answers will pre-fill the deep domain steps later.

fields.label: Project Name
fields.description: Working name for the project.

fields.label: Elevator Pitch
fields.placeholder: 2-3 sentences: what problem, for whom, why now
fields.description: This becomes the project elevator pitch in the domain deep-dive.

fields.label: Primary Persona
fields.placeholder: e.g. Game Master running TTRPG campaigns
fields.description: Who is the primary user? One sentence.

fields.label: 5 Key Domain Terms
fields.placeholder:
Campaign
Session
NPC
Setting
Dice Roll
fields.description: One term per line. These seed the domain glossary.

steps.label: Step 2 - Project Type & Stack
steps.description: Choose your project type to unlock relevant technology choices. Each selection maps to a specific rule-* skill.

fields.label: Project Type
fields.description: Draws from rule-platform-* skills: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Library, Agent, Backend, or Custom.

fields.label: Architecture Skill
fields.description: Choose the rule-* skill closest to your project type.

fields.label: Frontend Framework
fields.description: UI framework from rule-frontend-* skills. Shows when project type is Web or Desktop.

fields.label: Meta Framework (SSR/SSG)
fields.description: Full-stack framework built on the chosen frontend. Only available when Project Type is Web and a compatible frontend is selected.

fields.label: Desktop Framework
fields.description: Desktop application framework from rule-platform-desktop.

fields.label: Backend / API Framework
fields.description: Server framework from rule-backend-* skills. Shows when project needs a backend.

fields.label: Database Engine
fields.description: Persistence layer from rule-data-* skills. Shows when a backend framework is selected.

fields.label: API Style
fields.description: API contract pattern: REST, GraphQL, tRPC, WebSocket, or Local Only.

fields.label: CSS Approach
fields.description: CSS framework or methodology.

options.label: ESLint + Prettier - rule-toolchain-eslint
options.description: ESLint 9+ flat config + Prettier - full plugin ecosystem

fields.label: Technical Constraints
fields.description: Hard technical rules the implementation must honor. Framework-neutral - write what is true for your stack.

subfields.label: Constraint
subfields.placeholder: e.g. Zero runtime dependencies - platform APIs only, no production npm packages

steps.label: Step 3 - Stack Versions
steps.description: Pin major versions. Defaults are latest stable.

steps.label: Step 4 - Architecture Pattern
steps.description: Choose the high-level architecture pattern that best fits your project.

fields.label: Architecture Pattern

options.label: Layered
options.description: Presentation/Business/Persistence. Simple, well-understood, good for CRUD apps.

options.label: Clean Architecture
options.description: Dependency inversion with inner use-case layer. Good for complex business logic.

options.label: Hexagonal / Ports & Adapters
options.description: Domain core with pluggable adapters. Good for testability.

options.label: Domain-Driven Design
options.description: Ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, aggregates. For complex domains.

fields.description: Architecture pattern determines module organization, dependency direction, and testability.

fields.label: Architecture Principles
fields.description: Guiding principles this codebase holds to. Keep them true for YOUR stack - they render verbatim into the pack.

subfields.label: Principle
subfields.placeholder: e.g. Deterministic domain logic - business rules explicit and testable
